editorial:
Imagine traveling back in time to the chaos of the Vietnam War with Mark Gor, the coolest guy in Hong Kong cinema. You get to see a younger, rougher side of him as he heads into Saigon to save his family members. The vibe is a wild mix of war-zone tension and classic crime drama, where every corner holds a new threat. You will feel the heat and the noise of the city as Mark gets tangled up with a local gangster who is both a help and a headache. It is a gritty prequel that sets the stage for everything you love about the rest of the series.

What really hits home is the non-stop energy and the explosive gunfights that Tsui Hark is famous for. The acting is solid, though the plot can feel a bit messy if you try to overthink it. If you love old-school action with tons of bullets and big emotions, you need to see this. It is a great ride for anyone who misses the golden age of action movies.
endingExplained: The movie wraps up with a massive, bloody shootout as Mark and his allies try to escape the city. After fighting through waves of enemies, Mark manages to get his family to safety, but the cost is high. The ending shows that the violence of Saigon changed him, turning him into the hardened man you see in the first movie. He leaves the war behind, but the scars and the lessons of loyalty stay with him forever.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves 80s Hong Kong action and high-stakes shootouts.
